When I bought this, I thought it was about clicking on the button while it moved around the screen. The guns and whatnot would autoshoot and you had to "Just Click the Button", but this was not the case. Still I gave the product a chance, but there is a severe lack of content. There is no difficulty scaling up until the bosses, there are no mini-bosses and the whole thing feels very...mediocre. It's a good concept, in a better skin and with some more love, it could be amazing. PS (If the developer reads this): Getting different guns and melee weapons is too hard, using mini-boss system you can have players choose among new things to add to the button. This would allow for a lot more fun upgrades (which the game also lacks).

Developed and published by Simon Eftestol, Just Click The Button takes an intentionally simple concept and transforms it into an entertaining incremental experience packed with far more variety than its title initially suggests. The game begins with the most basic objective imaginable: repeatedly click a button. While this straightforward premise may seem too minimal to sustain long-term interest, it gradually reveals a surprisingly deep progression system that keeps introducing fresh mechanics, upgrades, and challenges. Every click contributes toward meaningful advancement, giving players a constant sense of accomplishment while encouraging them to see what new surprises lie ahead. The core gameplay revolves around steadily increasing your power through upgrades, unlockable abilities, and character progression. Instead of simply watching numerical values climb endlessly, players are given opportunities to shape their own approach by selecting different upgrades and building unique combinations of skills. This flexibility makes progression feel rewarding because every decision influences how future encounters unfold. The game successfully avoids becoming a mindless grind by consistently providing new goals and systems that expand upon the original mechanic rather than simply making the numbers larger. One of the game's most enjoyable features is how it blends incremental mechanics with fast-paced action. As players become stronger, the experience shifts beyond idle clicking into frantic arena-style encounters that borrow elements from reverse bullet hell games. Enemy waves, projectiles, and increasingly chaotic situations require active participation, creating an engaging contrast between strategic planning and moment-to-moment survival. This combination prevents the gameplay from becoming repetitive, as players must balance efficient progression with quick reactions while adapting their builds to overcome increasingly demanding situations. Replay value is another area where Just Click The Button performs exceptionally well. Rather than presenting a single path to completion, it offers multiple endings that encourage experimentation with different upgrade choices and playstyles. Players can aim to unlock every available ability, discover alternative routes, or simply continue pushing their character to greater levels of power. Because different builds can significantly alter the flow of each run, returning for another playthrough remains satisfying instead of feeling like a simple repetition of previous attempts. This variety helps extend the game's longevity well beyond what its modest premise might suggest. Visually, the game embraces a clean and colorful presentation that supports its fast-paced gameplay. The interface is easy to understand, allowing players to focus on progression without unnecessary complexity. As the action intensifies, the screen becomes filled with effects, enemies, and abilities that create an exciting sense of escalation. Although the growing visual chaos occasionally makes it difficult to track every detail, it also reinforces the feeling that the player has evolved from clicking a lone button into controlling an increasingly powerful force. The game's lighthearted tone complements this progression nicely, never taking itself too seriously while still delivering satisfying gameplay systems. Just Click The Button is not without limitations. The repetitive act of clicking remains central throughout the experience, so players who dislike incremental games may find it difficult to stay invested despite the additional mechanics. Some late-game moments can also become visually overwhelming due to the sheer number of effects occurring simultaneously. Nevertheless, these drawbacks are outweighed by the game's creative approach to expanding a simple concept into something much more engaging. Simon Eftestol demonstrates that a minimalist idea can support a surprisingly rich gameplay experience when paired with thoughtful progression and inventive design. By combining clicker mechanics, customizable builds, action-oriented combat, and multiple endings, Just Click The Button offers far more depth than its name implies. It succeeds as both a satisfying incremental game and an entertaining hybrid that rewards experimentation and persistence, making it an easy recommendation for players who enjoy watching simple mechanics evolve into something unexpectedly compelling. Rating: 8/10

Just Click The Button takes an incredibly simple concept and somehow turns it into a surprisingly addictive experience. What starts as literally clicking a single button quickly evolves into a mix of incremental progression, upgrades, and bullet-hell style gameplay that constantly keeps things interesting. The progression feels rewarding, with plenty of different abilities and builds to experiment with. Every upgrade feels meaningful, and it's satisfying watching your build become stronger as the chaos on screen ramps up. Despite its simple premise, there's a surprising amount of depth if you enjoy optimizing and trying different playstyles. The game also does a great job of introducing new mechanics at a steady pace, so it rarely feels repetitive. For such a simple idea, there's a lot more content than you'd expect, including multiple endings that encourage replaying with different builds. If you're a fan of clicker games, incremental games, or just want a fun indie title that doesn't overcomplicate itself, Just Click The Button is an easy recommendation. Overall rating: 8.5/10
